topic: AI personalization and loyalty in restaurants
angle: Personalization pays only when it’s tied to loyalty economics, not novelty.
linkedinPost:
Most “personalization” programs are just expensive ways to say hello by name.

A recent Knowledge at Wharton interview with WOWorks’ CMO highlights how fast-casual brands use differentiation, personalization, and loyalty to win repeat visits. The lesson applies well beyond restaurants: loyalty is a math problem before it’s a marketing one.

From the front lines, here’s what actually moves the needle with AI:

- Tie recommendations to contribution margin, not clicks. “Popular” isn’t profitable if it pushes the wrong items.
- Optimize for return visit within 14 days, not open rate. Frequency beats vanity.
- Personalize offers by operational reality. Don’t promote what the kitchen (or warehouse) can’t fulfill.
- Track cannibalization. A discounted upsell that replaces a full-price item isn’t growth.

Enterprises that treat AI like a loyalty P&L get results. Those that chase shiny journeys create bespoke experiences nobody repeats—and nobody measures.

My take: Start with three numbers—incremental margin per customer, days-to-return, and cost to serve—and make the model prove it can move all three. Then scale.

Where has your “personalization” actually changed customer behavior you can monetize? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
